articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Latest from Israel, Iran, and the Middle East
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Latest from Israel, Iran, and the Middle East
articles.content_orig:
Oil prices climbed Thursday on worries over a possible escalation in the Middle East conflict as the U.S. reportedly plans to resume strikes against Iran.
Brent crude futures rose 1.71% to $110.67 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude gained 1.42% to $98.53.
The U.S. and Israeli militaries have drawn up specific plans for renewed strikes on Iran after next month's midterm elections, The New York Times reported, citing unnamed U.S. officials. Planning for a "short but intensive" operation is progressing, The Times said.
The U.S. has also ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia.
State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott in a post on X said the order applies only to Saudi Arabia, citing increasing attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on civilian targets, after reports said that the U.S. had directed some staff in the wider Gulf region to leave.
The economic fallout from elevated oil prices, however, may be less severe than in previous decades, as consumers have become less vulnerable to energy shocks, according to David Wagner, head of equity and portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors.
"$100 oil today is very different than $100 oil, you know, 20, 30 years ago," Wagner said, noting that crude prices remain well below their inflation-adjusted historical highs.
He pointed to U.S. government data showing that gasoline accounted for roughly 5% of the average American's disposable income a decade ago, compared with about half that today, suggesting households may be better positioned to withstand elevated energy costs.
"I think we can hold that umbrella over our head ... from the rainstorm of oil," he said.
— CNBC's Anniek Bao contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Stock futures fall as investors digest earnings from Meta and Tesla: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stock futures fall as investors digest earnings from Meta and Tesla: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Tesla reported better-than-expected third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday, even as automotive revenue dropped. The stock slid more than 3% in extended trading.
Here's how the company did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:
Tesla's earnings report lands a day after CEO Elon Musk told investors on SpaceX's quarterly call that it would be a "good idea" for his two companies to merge, and said the boards at both have formed special committees to discuss a possible tie-up.
"I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield," Musk said on the call, responding to a question about a potential merger.
Musk addressed the matter in his opening comments on the Tesla call, but didn't provide any additional information.
"I think I said everything that should be said yesterday," he said.
Tesla's revenue was down slightly flat from a year earlier, when the company generated sales of $28.24 billion, according to the earnings deck. In Tesla's core automotive business, revenue declined 3% from a year earlier to $20.56 billion in the quarter. Energy revenue fell 16% to $2.88 billion.
Balancing out the declines were gains in Tesla's services and other revenue. Sales there climbed 33% from a year ago to $4.61 billion.
Tesla blamed its lackluster automotive revenue and profits on lower average sales prices for its cars during the quarter, and trouble securing battery supplies to make enough vehicles to fulfill a backlog of orders.
Net income attributable to common share holders plummeted 29% to $787 million, or 22 cents a share, from $1.11 billion, or 32 cents a share, a year earlier, Tesla said.
The drop in profitability reflects a surge in spending on Optimus humanoid robots and other artificial intelligence initiatives. Capital expenditures more than doubled from a year earlier to $3.73 billion. Free cash flow plunged by 62% year over year to $1.53 billion, after Tesla turned free cash flow negative in the second quarter.
Tesla said uptake of its FSD (Supervised), a partially automated driving system the company sells for $99 per month in the U.S., grew by 20 percentage points from the second quarter. Active FSD subscriptions increased 67% from a year earlier to 1.74 million.
"We believe that FSD is driving demand in markets where it is available, and we continue to work with regulators to get it approved in other markets," the company said in its investor deck.
Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's vice president of Autopilot, said on the earnings call that the company plans to give some customer cars access to its forthcoming FSD (Unsupervised) systems around the second quarter of next year.
Tesla is testing its Cybercab, a bronze two-seater designed for use as a robotaxi, but it's not yet sold to individuals. Musk said on the call that "the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and transport-as-a-service."
The company plans to bring Cybercab to cities beyond Austin, Texas, this year, Taneja said, paying attention to operating costs like maintenance, charging and cleaning.
Musk said the company's driverless Robotaxi fleet will start to contribute to the company's financials in 2027. That fleet now includes 362 Model Y Robotaxi, and 449 Cybercab vehicles authorized for driverless operations in Texas, according to the state's Department of Motor Vehicles,
"It's not like going to move the needle this quarter," Musk said, "I think it starts to become noticeable in Q2 and then probably a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year."
Barring regulatory intervention and protectionism, Musk predicted that Tesla "will end up doing a majority of all passenger miles on Earth in any country where it is allowed to operate freely."
Tesla said its auto sales in Canada, Japan, Taiwan and Australia hit new records during the quarter. However, the company has gotten meager growth out of its core market of late as Chinese EV makers such as BYD and Xiaomi gained popularity in Asia and Europe with affordable and innovative EVs. Tesla was also hit last year by the end of a federal EV tax credit.
Earlier this month, Tesla reported vehicle deliveries for the third quarter of 486,532, about 2% below the year-ago number. Deliveries are the closest approximation of sales reported by Tesla but are not precisely defined in its shareholder communications.
One of Tesla's big investments is in a semiconductor factory that it's building with SpaceX and Intel in Grimes County, Texas. That partnership with SpaceX along with other areas of overlap, including work on Tesla's recently announced Roadster refresh, fueled intensifying speculation that Musk's companies were on the verge of combining in what would be a historic transaction.
On Optimus, Musk said Tesla is "making good progress" on the AI systems that control the robots in development. He said there's "still quite a lot of work to do with regard to the AI and the robot for it to be truly useful for open-ended tasks."
Musk said he expects current issues around electromechanical design, reliability, usage duration, and AI to be "solved around the end of next year."

articles.title_orig: Why Chinese pundits say France’s riots could reshape European politics
articles.title_zh: Why Chinese pundits say France’s riots could reshape European politics
articles.content_orig:
Protests stem from falling competitiveness with an eroded middle class, providing ‘fertile ground’ for polarisation, observers say
The social unrest roiling France is being closely watched for a possible spillover effect beyond the country’s borders that could reshape European politics, Chinese analysts said.
The crisis is a major stress test for French politicians as they navigate deep-seated economic and societal tensions in the run-up to the country’s presidential election in April next year, according to the analysts.
A critical question was whether the riots would subside quickly or escalate into prolonged instability, they added, with political parties across the spectrum exploiting the upheaval to advance their electoral gains.

articles.title_orig: China's stock market sinks into bear territory as CSI 300 extends 10-week rout
articles.title_zh: China's stock market sinks into bear territory as CSI 300 extends 10-week rout
articles.content_orig:
China's benchmark CSI 300 index on Thursday entered bear-market territory, falling 20% from its June peak, as a prolonged sell-off in its equities deepens.
The index, which tracks 300 of the largest stocks listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen, has declined for 10 consecutive weeks and is down 2.6% so far this week, underscoring sustained pressure on Chinese equities, data from LSEG showed. The index was more than 1% lower Thursday.
Jordan Cvetanovski, chairman and CIO at Pella Funds, said China's equity market continues to face structural challenges, particularly as the world's second-largest economy grapples with the fallout from years of excess capacity and overinvestment.
"I think China is really struggling with reining in the problems that they've had in the past from the overbuild of capacity and other things," Cvetanovski told CNBC, pointing to challenges facing companies even in globally competitive industries such as batteries — a sector where he still sees select opportunities in China.
Chinese firms have been suffering from declining profit growth amid intense competition that has eroded margins and even invited the government to step in. In September, the country posted it's weakest growth in industrial profits this year.
The world's second-largest economy also posted its slowest growth in over three years in the second quarter, pressured by a multiyear slowdown in the property sector and extended weakness in consumer demand.
Shaun Rein, managing director at China Market Research Group, expects further selling pressure as geopolitical uncertainty, concerns over an artificial intelligence bubble and deteriorating consumer confidence weigh on investor sentiment.
China's large base of retail investors could also exacerbate market volatility, Rein said, as individual investors are prone to exiting the market faster during periods of uncertainty.
Unlike major markets such as the New York Stock Exchange, where retail investors account for about 20%-25% of trade volumes, China's retail investors drive 90% of daily trading, according to data provided by HSBC.
"For Chinese, it's about wealth preservation," Rein said, noting that investors are increasingly favoring safer assets such as time deposits amid a weakening property market and sluggish labor conditions.
While Rein expects increased pressure on markets, he said the sell-off has been excessive, pointing to resilient exports and signs of a recovery in property prices in China's largest cities.
"It's a crisis of confidence right now not a crisis in the economy," he said, predicting a strong rebound in Chinese equities in 2027.
Daniel Gerard, senior multi-asset strategist at State Street Markets, also struck a more optimistic tone, saying that China's growing capabilities in artificial intelligence could eventually draw global investors back into its equity market, even before corporate earnings recover.

articles.title_orig: Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
articles.title_zh: Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
articles.content_orig:
The internet’s mad scramble on Wednesday to patch a pair of critical vulnerabilities in PHP , a widely used web scripting language, was already too late to stop every attack, newly released details reveal.
Wednesday’s release of fixes for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP caused administrators and security staff to race to identify and patch vulnerable websites and apps, while attackers inevitably reverse engineered the fixes to learn how to exploit the flaws. Some governments and other groups even proactively took key websites down in anticipation of the release, so they wouldn't be targeted before they could apply the patches.
But in addition to detecting such active exploitation on Wednesday, research published Wednesday evening by Amazon Web Services indicates that at least one actor had started attempting to exploit the bugs—known collectively as PHP2Shell—on October 17, four days before Wednesday's public revelations.
AWS analysts spotted the October 17 exploitation on Wednesday while looking back at activity on one of their so-called honeypots, or intentionally vulnerable web servers or other digital lures that help researchers study attack methods and trends. The attempt came from an IP address that AWS says is linked to a “commercial anonymization network,” in other words a proxy network or VPN .
“While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure,” CJ Moses, AWS's chief information security officer, wrote in the research post.
Proof-of-concept exploits for PHP2Shell began emerging publicly on Wednesday, with some seeming to appear hours before the public disclosure at 10 am ET. In the hours leading up to the disclosure, AWS researchers say their honeypots were hit with multiple exploitation attempts anonymized using various providers and seemingly with various attack goals, likely indicating multiple different actors. “Technical analysis is ongoing, and it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems,” Moses wrote. He added that “PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.”
The PHP Foundation did not immediately respond to WIRED's request for comment.
Though it is unclear how the exploitation on October 17 happened or where it came from, AWS emphasizes that the findings underscore how coordinated vulnerability disclosure must evolve and speed up given global access to AI tools that can accelerate vulnerability analysis and allow less technically proficient actors to quickly develop new exploits.
“The time from patch to working exploit is shrinking for structural reasons,” Moses wrote. “In the past, most exploitation we observed came after a public proof of concept was released. A small number of capable actors built exploits, and everyone else waited for them. That dependency is weakening. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff or advisory into a working exploit. As a result, more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed.”

articles.title_orig: North Korea says it will resume propaganda broadcasts across border into South Korea
articles.title_zh: North Korea says it will resume propaganda broadcasts across border into South Korea
articles.content_orig:
North Korea has said it plans to resume broadcasting anti-South Korea propaganda along the armed border between the two countries, as Seoul urged Pyongyang to discuss easing tensions.
Kim Yo Jong, a senior North Korean official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Wednesday that North Korea will place loudspeakers along the entire border, following a visit with top military officials to fortifications along the contested frontier.
Kim warned Seoul of “the most horrible and distressing situation” if South Korea continued what Pyongyang calls interference in the North’s internal affairs.
She added in a follow-up statement on Thursday that North Korea would place “new counter means” on alert along the border, without elaborating, and have its loudspeakers on “standby” within days.
A landmine blast last month that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) between the two countries has ratcheted up tensions. Seoul accused North Korean troops of deliberately laying mines in the border zone as part of the North’s fortification work.
Kim had denied the allegation, calling the incident a South Korean fabrication. She said North Korean tactical units had taken up new positions, and accused South Korean troops of conducting warning broadcasts and firing warning shots at multiple locations near the border.
Seoul said the warning shots were fired as “legitimate and defensive measures”.
North Korea has been adding mines, barbed wire fences, anti-tank barriers and other fortifications to what is already one of the world’s most heavily armed borders.
South Korea’s Ministry of National Defence urged North Korea on Thursday to discuss measures to ease tension at the border and prevent any accidental military clash, its spokesperson said.
Pyongyang had cut off a military hotline with the South after declaring it would no longer seek dialogue or unification with what it called its “foe”.
Both North and South Korea have historically used loudspeakers to broadcast propaganda across the border, with South Korean broadcasts featuring K-pop music and news that have long irked Pyongyang and prompted tit-for-tat responses.
The two Koreas are separated by the DMZ, established after the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice.
North Korea has been reinforcing its side of the DMZ with mines, barriers and fencing since 2024 as it seeks to establish what it calls a permanent border with South Korea.

articles.title_orig: Tesla shares reverse course as robotics, chipmaking caution overshadows upbeat Q3
articles.title_zh: Tesla shares reverse course as robotics, chipmaking caution overshadows upbeat Q3
articles.content_orig:
The Tesla tokenized stock contract on Binance Futures was quoted at $380.40 at the October 21 observation, marking a 3.33% gain over the prior 24 hours. During that period, trading fluctuated between an intraday low of $364.35 and a high of $384.36, with the contract finishing in the upper portion of that range. Reported Binance Futures volume reached $191.3 million, indicating the move occurred alongside substantial traded activity rather than on light participation.
A key feature of the current setup is the contract’s positioning around the 200-day simple moving average, which is supplied at $377.59. With the latest price standing $2.81 above this level, the immediate issue is whether the contract can maintain this break or whether it will slip back below. The 200-day SMA is identified in the data as an important mean-reversion reference for equity-linked instruments, so price behavior around this threshold is central to the near-term technical picture.
All four supplied simple moving averages (SMAs) sit beneath the current contract price. The 7-day SMA is at $365.75, the 20-day at $372.89, the 50-day at $367.98, and the 200-day at $377.59. The 12-period exponential moving average (EMA) is reported at $370.73 and the 26-period EMA at $369.93, both also below the market. Trading above this entire moving average stack is consistent with a recovery phase, although the small cushion over the 200-day SMA means that a single volatile session could erase that advantage.
The Bollinger Band configuration adds further context. The upper band is supplied at $391.87, the middle band at $372.89, and the lower band at $353.92. The corresponding %B reading is 0.6978, calculated as (price minus lower band) divided by (upper band minus lower band). This value places the contract roughly 70% of the way from the lower to the upper band, with price trading above the midline and edging toward the upper band at $391.87. That upper band sits above the immediate resistance level of $388.39 but below the strong resistance cited at $396.38, defining a relatively tight overhead region where supply may emerge.
The supplied 14-period relative strength index (RSI) is 57.72, which is explicitly classified as neutral. This level leaves room for additional upside before typical overbought zones are approached, while not, on its own, pointing to a strong directional edge.
The moving average convergence divergence (MACD) readings show the MACD line and its signal line both at 0.8080, producing a histogram value of 0.0000. The data labels this configuration as bearish momentum. A histogram print at zero indicates the spread between MACD and its signal line has been fully compressed. The next move in the histogram – whether it turns positive or negative – is described as the most sensitive element of the momentum profile for anticipating near-term price behavior.
The Stochastic oscillator is reported with %K at 79.50 and %D at 63.60, so %K is above %D. The %K value is near the 80 zone, an area where the oscillator has historically been watched for potential rollovers, while the fact that %K is above %D is, in itself, a bullish configuration in the short term. The daily 14-period average true range (ATR) is $11.54, illustrating that both the distance to the next identified resistance and to the nearest support fall within roughly one typical day’s expected range.

articles.title_orig: Phantom Blade Zero launch trailer, PS5 physical editions launch in 2027
articles.title_zh: Phantom Blade Zero launch trailer, PS5 physical editions launch in 2027
articles.content_orig:
S-GAME has released the launch trailer for Wuxia action RPG Phantom Blade Zero , as well as announced that physical standard, Deluxe, and Ultimate editions will launch for PlayStation 5 in 2027.
Here is an overview of the game, via S-GAME:
S-GAME presents Phantom Blade Zero , a fusion of classic Wuxia storytelling and exhilarating action powered by Unreal Engine 5. You play as Soul, a warrior with only sixty-six days left to live. Fend off assassins, unravel world-ending conspiracies, and defend your values with your life.
Framed for the death of his master and left with a ruined heart, Soul has sixty-six days to live. Alone and hunted by his former comrades, he moves through a world of shifting loyalties and silent blades—determined to unravel the conspiracy that has condemned him.
Rain mixes with blood, mercy entangles with vengeance. Soul’s journey is one of love, hate, and the fragile search for what it means to have a heart.
A Masterful Blend of Traditional Wuxia, Fantasy, and Folk Horror
Explore a world beyond imagination. Shifting realities, echoes of memories long since passed, augmentation, and beings of higher power await in Phantom Blade Zero .
A rumor, a story, a whisper—every thread a trail to unraveling a larger mystery. Navigate through a web of intrigue and lies to uncover the truth.
An Extensive Arsenal is at Your Disposal
A fighter’s worth lies in their weapons.
Over thirty weapons are yours to wield, with more than twenty unique “Phantom Edges” to mix and match to suit your playstyle.
Defeat powerful foes to obtain their weapons, and with it, their signature techniques. Grow your arsenal and defeat all who stand in your path.
Inspired by the Golden Age of Hong Kong action films, the world of Phantom Blade Zero blends fierce martial arts with machinery, amplifying an exhilarating clash of steel on steel.
Ancient codes meet iron and smoke; tradition thrums to a modern beat. A new style is forged in this melding of mediums. This is Kungfupunk.
An Authentic Kungfu Experience
Built in Unreal Engine 5 and through the use of state-of-the-art motion capture, Phantom Blade Zero brings together legendary fight choreography from Hong Kong’s Golden Age of martial arts cinema.
Every strike and stance draws from authentic martial arts techniques, captured with the precision of film, is reborn through modern game design.
This is Chinese kungfu reimagined for a new generation.
Phantom Blade Zero is due out for PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store on October 29.

articles.title_orig: Meta strikes deal to keep Zuckerberg in California after wealth tax concerns
articles.title_zh: Meta strikes deal to keep Zuckerberg in California after wealth tax concerns
articles.content_orig:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg intends to maintain control over the company he founded in 2004 and a new class of stock will help him do just that.
On Wednesday as Meta released third quarter earnings results, the company announced that it would issue a new share class of Class C stock. The share class, which is technically a one-for-one stock dividend of new Class C shares, will be distributed to all shareholders. It was conceived following months of extensive negotiation that grew contentious at times between Zuckerberg and board members, including DoorDash CEO Tony Xu, Ambassador Robert Kimmitt, and ex- Microsoft executive Charles Songhurst. Xu disclosed his personal friendship with Zuckerberg but said it wouldn’t impair his judgement. At one point, the committee even talked about resigning if they couldn’t come to a resolution.
According to a Meta filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, Zuckerberg wanted to be able to maintain his voting control, meet his pledges to fund the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative with his Meta stock, and be prepared to pay billions to the state of California if a proposed wealth tax is approved by voters in November.
The proposed wealth tax, however, came around the same time as a decision by the company in late 2025 that Meta needed to raise outside capital to help fund the AI boom. Zuckerberg holds about 60.6% of voting control at Meta, while his stake is about 13.4% of the company.
Like other major tech companies, Meta maintains a dual-class share structure, where Class A shares trade on Nasdaq as a one-vote-one-share stock. Conversely, Zuckerberg’s holdings are made up of mostly Class B shares, which carry 10 votes per share, which is how he maintains majority control. The condition on the supercharged Class B shares is if Zuckerberg sells them, they convert to Class A. Many companies require this condition for super-voting shares to ensure that outsiders don’t start to gain control of companies from founders seeking liquidity.
The rub is if Meta issues more Class A shares, which it does in order to make equity grants to employees, make acquisitions or raise capital, Zuckerberg’s stake gets diluted. Meta has long offset the dilution with stock buybacks, which helped buoy his voting power from 53.7% in 2013 to 60.6% now. But the buybacks also drain cash that Meta wants to use to fund the AI buildout. The company’s SEC filings show Meta repurchased $26.3 billion in Class A stock in 2025, but hasn’t bought back any shares in four straight quarters. Meanwhile, in the first nine months of this year, Meta posted $21 billion in stock-based compensation.
Meta’s third quarter results , released Wednesday, help explain why the share class came about. Revenue this quarter rose 26% to $64.6 billion while capital expenditures hit $34.9 billion. Meanwhile, free cash flow dipped to negative $2.1 billion, compared to $10.6 billion a year ago. Meta also forecast capex for 2026 at $135 billion to $140 billion, raising the low end up from $130 billion. Meta forecast fourth quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion.
As a solution to the crunch, the new Class C stock will carry no votes, the company said. Meta will use them to pay employees, fund acquisitions, and raise capital without Zuckerberg losing majority voting control. He can also sell some of them without giving up votes, and more importantly, pay a potentially massive wealth tax bill looming in California without having to tap into his Class B shares. His current level of control is such that he can personally elect all the directors on the board and determine most of the issues proposed to shareholders for a vote, which won’t change following the recapitalization. With the new shares, Zuckerberg can sell 20% right away, and the remaining 80% are “stapled”—meaning he can sell them only if he sells or converts an equal number of his voting shares.
Proposition 40 in California, known as the wealth tax, is up for a vote on Nov. 3 and if it passes, it could hit Zuckerberg and the wealthiest in the state with a multibillion bill. The Bloomberg Billionaires index lists him at #5 with a net worth of $246 billion. In July, Zuckerberg told Kimmitt, who is Meta’s lead independent director, that selling his Class B stock to cover what he might owe for the wealth tax could cut his voting stake back down to 53%.
The tax came up in a conversation between the two after negotiations between Zuckerberg and the committee appeared to grow tense. The committee had suggested shareholder-friendly sunset provisions that would see the Class B shares convert into regular stock within a year of Zuckerberg’s eventual death or departure from Meta—or if he sold more than half his holdings. During a call with Kimmitt in July, the two discussed the wealth tax and noted that Zuckerberg had only taken a $1 salary from Meta since 2013.
Later that same month, Zuckerberg again brought up Prop 40, this time raising concerns about whether it might impact his ability to stay a California resident. The following week, Zuckerberg’s lawyers sent a letter asking for a pay package similar to those made to other tech founders, partly so Zuckerberg could pay a potential tax bill. Like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, many founders in tech have moonshot performance pay packages, in which rigorous stock price growth is tied to massive pay hurdles. According to the filing, Zuckerberg refused to consider any changes to his voting shares, including sunset provisions, and told the committee he was “considering establishing residence outside of California.”
The next day, the committee hashed over Zuckerberg’s stance and went over Meta’s analyst coverage and commentary, and the tightening of credit conditions for hyperscalers. Meta had seen  relatively looser demand for its July bond issuance for a Texas data center. The committee wanted to keep Zuckerberg in California, close to its artificial intelligence lab.
Later that same day, August 4, Zuckerberg proposed a dividend of 20 shares of Class C stock for each share of Class A and B shares, paid to all shareholders. He told the committee he wouldn’t agree to sunsetting his Class Bs or support equity financing that diluted his voting control.
Then, he upped the stakes.
Zuckerberg told the committee “he intended to establish residence outside California, which he had been advised he would need to do before the November. 3, 2026 election,” the filing states.
The committee met again August 5, but viewed the 20-for-1 proposal as “excessive,” the filing states. By late August, all sides were dug in after various proposals had been issued and objected to. Eventually, committee members discussed dissolving the committee or resigning from the board if Zuckerberg wouldn’t make concessions for the benefit of all Class A shareholders.
At a September 9 board dinner, Zuckerberg told directors he planned to list his Palo Alto estate for sale on September 13. Committee members had recused themselves from dinner during his update. And then within days, a new proposal came together. Zuckerberg dropped his pay request and agreed to keep the $1 salary and committed to stay in California or wherever Meta is headquartered, for eight years. All shareholders get another one-for-one Class C dividend every time the stock price doubles from $580.60, so long as annual returns are at least 10%.
The deal was inked on September 14. Every Class A and Class B share will get one Class C share, effectively a two-for-one split and Zuckerberg can sell 20% of his new Class C shares right away. The committee approved days before the full board sealed the deal on October 19. Chan Zuckerberg entities that hold 56% of the vote signed off the following day and the new shares take effect on Jan. 19, 2027.
Chief financial officer Susan Li said Wednesday trading of the Class C stock will begin in late January. She said Meta has no specific financing plans yet.

articles.title_orig: A look at the major candidates in Israel’s election Tuesday
articles.title_zh: A look at the major candidates in Israel’s election Tuesday
articles.content_orig:
An N12 News poll published Wednesday evening ranked Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party first with 23 seats, down one seat from the previous poll. A Channel 13 poll published at the same time also put Yashar in first place; however they only received 20 seats.
In both polls, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party came in second, trailing Yashar and falling to 19 seats.
Neither poll found that either of the political blocs would win a clear majority; however, the opposition bloc continued to lead Netanyahu's.
N12 projected that the opposition bloc would win 55 seats and Netanyahu's bloc 51. By comparison, the Channel 13 poll showed Eisenkot's bloc gaining one seat to 52, while Netanyahu's bloc lost one seat to 49.
Whether Ofer Winter's People of Israel party and Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha's Reservists-Economic Party cross the 3.25% electoral threshold could affect the balance between the political blocs in the upcoming elections.
Former prime minister Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad party remained unchanged at 14 seats, while the Democrats, led by Yair Golan, gained one seat to reach 10, Channel 13 found. In N12, the Democrats remained at nine seats, while B'Yachad gained one seat to reach 15, its highest showing in a month and a half.
In both polls, Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu polled at eight seats, and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit received seven.
Shas, led by Arye Deri, received eight seats in the N12 poll but seven on Channel 13, while United Torah Judaism, led by Yakov Asher, received seven in the N12 poll but eight on Channel 13.
The Religious Zionist Party (RZP) and Zehut, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Moshe Feiglin, received six seats in the N12 poll, which rose to eight in the Channel 13 poll.
The Joint List , comprising Hadash, Ta'al, and Balad and led by Yousef Jabareen, received nine seats in both polls; however, N12 found that Mansour Abbas's Ra'am was polling at five, while Channel 13 placed Ra'am at 6. In both polls, the Arab parties remained stable, earning the same number of seats as in the previous poll.
In the N12 poll, the People of Israel party won four seats, crossing the electoral threshold after falling below it in the previous two polls. However, the Reservists-Economic Party remained below the electoral threshold with 2.8% of the vote.
In contrast, the Channel 13 poll reversed the two. The Reservists-Economic Party kept its four seats and remained above the electoral threshold. Meanwhile, the People of Israel party fell below the electoral threshold after receiving four seats in the previous poll.
A pollster for The Madad and Channel 13 News spoke with 103FM about the latest Channel 13 poll, explaining how the results of the two parties could affect the distribution of Knesset seats between the blocs.
Addressing a scenario in which one or both parties fail to cross the electoral threshold, he explained which bloc could benefit from the redistribution of seats.
"In terms of the balance between the blocs, if neither crosses the threshold, eight seats can be redistributed among other parties. However, one scenario is that one fails to cross the threshold and the other does, leaving four seats to be redistributed. Which party fails to cross the threshold could be significant. The side that would benefit more would be what we call the 'change bloc,' rather than the coalition bloc," he said, adding, "That is the conclusion we reached."
He also addressed where the two parties draw their support from and the differences between voters backing Winter and those supporting Hendel and Zelekha.
"People of Israel and the Reservists receive votes from both sides in almost equal measure. The question is when we start counting, whether we use the 2022 election as our starting point and ask where those votes were in the previous election," he explained.
"It is true that Hendel and Zelekha's votes come more evenly from both sides, while most of Winter's votes come from the coalition side. Nevertheless, Winter also took roughly one seat, out of the nearly four he has, from the opposition side, mainly from Liberman's party," he added.

articles.title_orig: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
articles.title_zh: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
articles.content_orig:
The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia as attacks escalate, with three people killed in strikes across the country.
Saudi authorities said debris from a drone intercepted during an attempted attack on an oil field killed two people, while one person died after a strike at the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
Conflict between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia has been rising in the past month.
The Houthis have responded to Saudi strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in Saudi Arabia. A recent strike on Riyadh's international airport was the deadliest in the kingdom in years.
"The US Department of State issued an ordered departure for non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia," a state department spokesperson said in a statement.
"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," it added.
The spokesperson also warned "the hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly".
In the latest attack on the King Fahd International Airport eight people sustained injuries that ranged from "minor to serious", officials said.
No details of the attack have yet been given, but the strike comes after airports in Saudi Arabia have been repeatedly targeted by Houthi forces.
The energy ministry has also not said who had launched the drone aimed at the Shaybah oil field near the border with the United Arab Emirates that left two people injured.
Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa, in 2014. Conflicts escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led military coalition tried to restore the government's rule.
An informal ceasefire had been in place for the past four years, but it unravelled in July after the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.
The group's "maritime embargo" in the Bab al-Mandab Strait along Yemen's south-western coast has contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

articles.title_orig: Tesla profits fall on higher spending as 'Elon Inc.' talk builds
articles.title_zh: Tesla profits fall on higher spending as 'Elon Inc.' talk builds
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Tesla reported lower third-quarter profits Wednesday as near-trillionaire Elon Musk's electric vehicle maker ramped up huge investments in artificial intelligence and other envelope-pushing technologies.
Besides marginally lower car sales, Tesla saw a drop in revenues from regulatory credits and energy and storage, while spending on research and development more than doubled as the company engages in a spending binge on AI, robotics and autonomous transport.
The earnings were arguably upstaged by Musk's disclosure Tuesday that special committees of independent directors at both SpaceX and Tesla have been set up to discuss a merger of the two companies. Musk, who leads both companies, declined to offer further details Wednesday.
The potential merger -- which some have dubbed "Elon Inc." -- boosted shares of both companies on Wednesday, lifting Musk's wealth back near $1 trillion at $989 billion, according to Forbes' real-time billionaires index.
In the third quarter, Tesla reported profits of $787 million, down 42.7 percent from the year-ago period. Revenues were essentially flat at $28 billion.
Analysts had been cautious about Tesla's latest results heading into Wednesday's release.
While third-quarter auto sales topped estimates, due in part to an uptick in European markets amid high gasoline prices, better sales have not always translated to Tesla's bottom line.
The company has faced questions about the rollout of Tesla's robotaxi venture that has progressed much more slowly than hoped.
Musk has repeatedly made overly rosy forecasts about self-driving technology, as in 2019 when he predicted there would be more than a million robotaxis the following year.
In Texas, where Tesla has focused its robotaxi launch, there are currently about 800 robotaxis, according to FSD Database.
Tesla's release highlighted the September 3 launch of robotaxi service in Austin and said "cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew eightfold quarter over quarter."
Company officials said Wednesday that if the current pace of robotaxi growth continues, the venture could be meaningful financially as early as next year. The ramp-up is guided by a strong desire to avoid safety problems, company officials said.
For much of this year, Tesla has also encountered scrutiny over swelling capital spending to fund ambitious programs in artificial intelligence, robotics and autonomous driving.
Capital spending more than doubled in the third quarter to $4.7 billion, but the company lowered its capital spending plans compared with earlier in the year.
Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja, who in July had projected 2026 spending of more than $25 billion, said Wednesday the company expects to spend $20 billion, adding that the company managed "our capital deployment efficiently."
That is still more than double Tesla's 2025 capital budget of $8.5 billion.
Besides robotaxi and AI, Tesla is heavily investing in Musk's "Optimus" humanoid robots as well as the buildout jointly with SpaceX of a large chip factory in Austin.
The chip factory, called Terafab, was the object of some of Musk's most effusive and self-boosting language on Wednesday.
"Terafab I think will be the most valuable building in the world, and will probably have an economic value that will place it in the top 20 of countries," he said.
Musk is also eyeing auto growth, projecting production of five million in 2030 compared with 1.7 million in 2025.
"After many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth," Musk said.
- Looming SpaceX merger? -
But questions about Tesla's future loomed larger with talk of the potential SpaceX tie-up. The companies have a combined equity value of more than $3.5 trillion.
"We think it's a matter of when, not if" the two companies combine, said CFRA Research equity analyst Garrett Nelson.
"That's the whole issue," Nelson said of a potential megadeal. "Tesla as we know it today may not exist in six to 12 months."
On SpaceX's conference call Tuesday night, Musk said the committees have not agreed on the terms of any deal and there is no guarantee they will.
Musk said the two companies could gain from working together on AI software, chip design, robotics and space-based computing.
Talk of the deal heaps additional attention on Musk as the billionaire's latest cash infusion into US political elections fuels fresh criticism. Musk has steered at least $276 million to allies of President Donald Trump in the Republican Party.
Musk is also under scrutiny over a report he ordered a reduction in Starshield telecom services for Ukraine, adding to pressure on the country at the same time Trump has criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and called for him to be replaced.
Shares of Tesla initially rose in after-hours trading, but were down 3.3 percent near 0050 GMT.

articles.title_orig: Dusky shark that became a tourist draw while trapped in a South Korean canal finally swims free
articles.title_zh: Dusky shark that became a tourist draw while trapped in a South Korean canal finally swims free
articles.content_orig:
A famed dusky shark in South Korea has returned to the canal where she had been stuck for a month, just one day after authorities said they had successfully guided her out, local media report.
The shark, nicknamed Bukangi, became an unlikely sensation after she was spotted lingering in a canal in the south-eastern port city of Busan last month.
South Korea's oceans ministry said on Wednesday evening they had led Bukangi out of the canal into an open harbour - but reports later said the shark had swum back to the mouth of the canal, having apparently broken through a barrier installed by authorities.
Another operation to relocate Bukangi has been scheduled for Thursday.
It is thought that Bukangi might have been drawn to the canal by unusually warm waters and plenty of fish. With the sea getting warmer each year, experts say Busan may play host to more sharks in the future.
In recent weeks, more than 1.6 million visitors have descended upon a park in Busan to catch a glimpse of Bukangi, named after the canal in which she was spotted.
Her popularity gave a welcome boost to Busan's tourism, and the city has embraced her as an unofficial mascot.
But authorities were also concerned about Bukangi's well-being as she appeared to be injured and was not eating. Social media users have been circulating videos of Bukangi swimming in the canal with what appears to be a bloodied snout.
There were concerns that she would be further weakened by falling water temperatures.
In a livestreamed operation on Wednesday, rescue workers took more than eight hours to delicately guide the three-metre-long (10ft) shark with a net towards open water in a harbour.
Hundreds of adoring fans cheered and waved goodbye to their shark, unaware that she would still be lingering in the canal by the next day.
Before Wednesday's operation, there had been two earlier failed attempts to guide Bukangi out of the canal with nets.

articles.title_orig: Heidi Levine recounts how Palestinian youths helped save her in settler attack
articles.title_zh: Heidi Levine recounts how Palestinian youths helped save her in settler attack
articles.content_orig:
US photojournalist describes ‘protective shield’, vows to return to work in West Bank and criticises Netanyahu comments on incident
The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers in the West Bank on Friday has described how she was saved with the help of local Palestinians.
Heidi Levine sustained four fractured vertebrae, two broken ribs and four puncture wounds when she was knocked to the ground and repeatedly beaten by a crowd of masked settlers while she and other journalists were covering the olive harvest in the Palestinian village of Abu Falah, north of Ramallah.
It is unclear whether the puncture wounds were caused by knives or other weapons. Levine said a witness to her attack had seen nails sticking out of some of the wooden clubs wielded by her attackers.
Levine, 64, has covered multiple wars and had just returned from an assignment in Ukraine before Friday’s attack. She said she would most likely have been killed had she not been wearing protective body armour and a helmet.
“I probably would have been dead, because for sure it doesn’t take much to kill a person with blows to the head,” she said shortly before being discharged from hospital on Wednesday in the Israeli city of Petah Tikva.
Levine pointed out that Palestinians did not have such protection and more than 20 had been killed in settler attacks so far this year, in the course of an escalating campaign of aggression – described as terrorism by Israeli security leaders – across the West Bank, aimed at driving Palestinians from their land.
“Every single journalist who looked at [the attack on me] are thinking they and I have gone to so many funerals of Palestinians killed by settlers,” Levine said.
She said the olive harvesting at Abu Falah had begun peacefully but at some point a group of young masked settlers appeared on a nearby hilltop watching the group of Palestinian villagers, journalists and human rights activists accompanying them. Levine said the attack began only after the Israeli army arrived on the scene.
“Then all hell broke loose. Some of the farmers started to gather their tarps and bags of olives that they had picked,” she said. “Then all of a sudden I hear a machine gun, and then saw teargas in the distance. I started to run … It was just like a lot of commotion and then all of a sudden I see a dozen of them and they started charging at me.
“I managed to keep my face to the ground, and I don’t know if I took that position to protect myself with my face down or it was their initial blow. Otherwise my whole face would have been broken and I could have suffered brain damage or lost an eye.
“They started kicking me and beating me with sticks. I can’t even count how many times, probably more than a hundred times. I actually tried playing dead so that they would stop. But it didn’t work.”
Witnesses said the beating only ceased when young Palestinian men used slingshots to aim stones at settlers forcing them back, allowing another American journalist, Jasper Nathaniel, to reach Levine and, with other reporters, help her to safety.
“The shabab [Palestinian youth] put themselves in front and were trying to keep them [the settlers] away, keep a protective shield, which was amazing. It was like a biblical battle,” Levine said.
After the attack, Nathaniel wrote : “Had the shabab not stepped up to protect her, she might well be dead. It is no exaggeration to say that young Palestinians armed only with stones risked their lives to save Heidi Levine’s.”
He said the army pursued the young Palestinians after the incident, rather than the settlers. Palestinians risk being shot by settlers or soldiers if they try to resist attacks, and can face long periods in detention without charge.
Levine, who has lived in Israel for four decades, said she would go back to reporting on the West Bank as soon as she recovered. “My work is important,” she said. “They have bruised me, broken some bones, but they haven’t cracked my spirit.”
Since the attack, she has received letters from Israelis expressing regret, and an apologetic phone call from the president, Isaac Herzog.
“He was a teddy bear on the phone,” she said. “He kept saying I just want to give you a big hug and these are not representative of who this country is, they’re a dark stain, and he called them thugs.”
The office of the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, however, put out a statement on X seeking to cast doubt on witness and video accounts of what he called an “alleged attack”.
Levine was particularly angered by Netanyahu’s claim that some video footage “appears to show Levine knocked down and immediately helped to her feet by the same unidentified individual”.
“That’s such bullshit. They helped me up because they couldn’t get my things off of me. That’s why,” Levine said. “They robbed me of everything I have – a pouch with my documents, my American passport, credit card, camera disk and a small camera bag with two other lenses. Everything is gone … That’s why [they stood me up], and then they threw me back down and continued to kick and hit me.”
The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, called the attack a “despicable act of terror” and demanded prosecutions. Israeli police arrested 10 suspects after the Abu Falah incident and another attack on Saturday aimed at European diplomats near the West Bank village of Taybeh.
On Wednesday an Israeli court released four suspects in the attack on Levine and put them under house arrest, on the grounds there was insufficient evidence to keep them in custody.
Asked if she expected her attackers to be brought to justice, Levine said her level of confidence was “two out of 10”.
“I am not very hopeful,” she said. “Of course, if the government made the decision to do something and crack down on this and get people arrested, they would do it. But it’s not just arresting these teenage thugs. It’s going after their leaders, the rabbis, and how they’re organised.”

articles.title_orig: Musk Tries to Lock In His Tesla-SpaceX Dream Before Trump’s Exit
articles.title_zh: Musk Tries to Lock In His Tesla-SpaceX Dream Before Trump’s Exit
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together .
Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes."
The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.
With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.
Any deal would also need shareholder backing. But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.
"In my opinion, 100%. It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group.
During Tesla's earnings call on Wednesday, Musk said he had nothing further to add about the prospect of a merger but quipped: "I feel like I'm tap-dancing through a minefield."
Musk said that calling the merger a certainty would be "overstating" things.
Tesla reported a slight drop in third quarter sales which came in at $28.05 billion compared with $28.1 billion at the same time last year.
The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.
Musk, chief executive of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.
Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.
The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.
Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.
But the merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, with half of Tesla's needed to back the deal, a threshold even Musk described as "quite a high hurdle".
Musk, as boss of both companies, cannot participate in shareholder discussions.
Even so, Musk, a key shareholder of Tesla, will likely get his way in the next few years, said investment analyst Dan Sheehan from Telos Wealth Advisors.
He believes shareholders will back the deal as the technology the companies develop complement each other, Sheehan said.
But the merger would mean that Tesla shareholders will likely hold a "smaller slice of a much larger and more complex business," he added.
"There's no real precedent for how a public company like Tesla gets priced in this," Sheehan said.
SpaceX shares rose 8% in after hours trading while shares of Tesla climbed by 2%.
Experts told the BBC that Tesla drivers are unlikely to see much drastic change in the near term, even if the two companies combine.
In fact, vehicles seem almost like "an afterthought", overshadowed by the potential to combine the Tesla and SpaceX's tech capabilities, Nicholson said.
Changes are already underway at Tesla. The carmaker said earlier this year that it would prioritise its best-selling Model Y and Model 3, shifting focus away from less popular models .
Tesla also started using a manufacturing plant in California to produce humanoid robots, known as Optimus.
Pairing Tesla's self-driving technology and robotics with SpaceX's AI and satellite network could result in more capable vehicles, Sheehan said.
"The question is how much priority cars get inside a company increasingly driven by AI infrastructure," he added.
The recent Roadster showcase suggests SpaceX technology could be pulled into future Tesla products, which could attract more customers, said Tu Le, the founder of advisory firm Sino Auto Insights.
The Cybertruck-maker faces intense competition from Chinese carmakers like BYD, which overtook Tesla as the world's biggest EV maker in January.
The biggest winner is probably Musk - the world's richest man who also became the world's first trillionaire earlier this year.
The merger would give Musk greater voting control over the combined company than he currently has at Tesla, a factor the special committee assessing the deal would have to consider.
A single company makes it easier for Musk to run his AI strategy the way he wants, Sheehan said.
"The deal itself doesn't add to Musk's wealth, but it concentrates it further in one stock," he said.
However, the merger could attract scrutiny over Musk, already a polarising figure in the US, Nicholson said.
The move could also face more regulatory pressure if Democrats - many of whom have been critical of Musk - win more seats in the US midterm elections next month.
Shareholders have backed Musk's desires before. Last year, Tesla investors approved an unprecedented compensation package for Musk valued around $1tn .
"I honestly don't think Musk will be keeping track of what the merger will do for his wealth," Nicholson said.
The deal also brings Musk closer to what Nicholson says is "his mission in life": colonising Mars.

articles.title_orig: Musk Says Tesla Aims to Begin Humanoid Robot Sales Next Year
articles.title_zh: Musk Says Tesla Aims to Begin Humanoid Robot Sales Next Year
articles.content_orig:
In a statement that underscores a shift in Tesla ’s ( NASDAQ: TSLA ) strategic priorities, Elon Musk has emphasized that the company’s humanoid robot Optimus and its purpose-built autonomous Cybercab vehicle are expected to account for the vast majority of Tesla ’s future enterprise value.
The remarks, made in a reply on X , position advanced artificial intelligence and autonomous transportation as the true engines of long-term growth, rather than traditional electric vehicle sales or niche performance models.
Musk ’s comments came in response to a post by the account Teslaconomics, which suggested that observers fixated solely on the commercial prospects and profit margins of Tesla’s forthcoming Roadster were overlooking a larger opportunity.
Addressing that perspective directly, Musk stated that Optimus and Cybercab will constitute the overwhelming share of the company’s worth.
He elaborated that only a limited set of domains possess the potential to expand to truly extraordinary economic scales—those corresponding to what he termed “K2 and beyond.”
These include super intelligence, robots, solar power , and the capacity for mass transport to space.
In Musk’s framing, success in the first two areas—super intelligence and robotics—would naturally enable progress in the others.
This outlook reframes Tesla less as a conventional automaker and more as a platform for scalable AI-driven systems.
Optimus, the bipedal robot designed for general-purpose labor, and Cybercab, the steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle intended for robotaxi fleets, represent the practical embodiments of that vision.
By highlighting their expected dominance in valuation , Musk is signaling that investors should evaluate Tesla primarily through the lens of physical AI and unsupervised mobility rather than quarterly vehicle deliveries alone.
The implication is that once Tesla masters high-volume robotics and robust autonomous driving intelligence, adjacent opportunities in energy generation and space logistics become more attainable.
Musk also addressed the Roadster itself, acknowledging its limited role in the broader value equation while affirming that development will continue.
He described the vehicle as “super cool,” indicating that the project proceeds for reasons of engineering enthusiasm and brand appeal even if it is not expected to drive the majority of long-term valuation.
The distinction reinforces the hierarchy he outlined: exciting consumer products may persist, but the scalable foundations of super intelligence and robotics are what will define Tesla’s economic trajectory.
Optimus and Cybercab will be the vast majority of Tesla’s value.
The only things that will scale to incredible size (K2 and beyond) economically are super intelligence, robots, solar power and mass to space.
And, of course, if you have the first two, the rest will follow.…
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 18, 2026
The timing of the statement is notable.
It arrives as market attention turns toward Tesla’s upcoming earnings report, where updates on robotaxi operations and Optimus manufacturing progress are likely to draw significant scrutiny alongside traditional financial metrics.
Popular investor questions have already focused on plans to expand Cybercab fleets beyond initial markets and on the production costs associated with each Optimus unit.
Musk’s remarks effectively set expectations that these initiatives, rather than incremental improvements to existing vehicle lines, will determine the company’s trajectory in the years ahead.
By centering AI and autonomous transportation, Musk is articulating a coherent long-term thesis.
Super intelligence provides the cognitive backbone for both humanoid robots that can perform diverse physical tasks and fleets of vehicles that operate without human drivers.
In this view, the economic potential of such systems far exceeds that of conventional automotive manufacturing.
The statement does not include specific revenue projections, timelines, or valuation models, leaving the precise scale of the opportunity open to interpretation.
Yet the directional clarity is unmistakable: Tesla’s future value, according to its chief executive, will be generated predominantly by Optimus and Cybercab.
This perspective continues a pattern of elevating robotics and autonomy above legacy vehicle businesses.
It invites stakeholders to assess progress not merely by units sold or margins achieved in traditional segments, but by the rate at which AI capabilities mature and autonomous systems reach volume production.
As Tesla advances its capital plans for robot and robotaxi manufacturing, Musk’s latest comments provide a clear framework for understanding where the company intends to concentrate its efforts and where it expects the majority of future value to emerge.

articles.title_orig: See Super Typhoon Champi’s giant eye as it swirls across the Pacific
articles.title_zh: See Super Typhoon Champi’s giant eye as it swirls across the Pacific
articles.content_orig:
Super Typhoon Champi, which is barreling across the western Pacific Ocean, became one of the strongest storms on Earth in 2026 on Wednesday.
The tropical cyclone tied April's Super Typhoon Sinlaku for the strongest 1-minute sustained winds of 2026, at 185 mph, which is equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane.
Hurricanes and typhoons are both tropical cyclones with sustained winds of at least 74 mph.
"A tropical cyclone is a generic term used by meteorologists to describe a rotating, organized system of clouds and thunderstorms that originates over tropical or subtropical waters and has closed, low-level circulation," according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration .
The main difference between hurricanes and typhoons is geographic: Storms in the Northwest Pacific are called typhoons, while those in the North Atlantic and central and eastern North Pacific are called hurricanes.
The Joint Typhoon Warning Center classifies a storm as a super typhoon when its 1-minute sustained winds reach at least 150 mph. That threshold falls within the Category 4 hurricane range.
Champi is currently east of the Philippines and southeast of Taiwan, moving west-northwest across the Philippine Sea at 15 mph. Maximum sustained winds are at 175 mph, after peaking at 185 mph, according to the latest update from the National Weather Service .
The storm is forecast to make a slight turn toward the northwest and weaken through Thursday.
Super Typhoon Champi's path.
Champi is expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Taiwan and eastern China through the weekend, according to AccuWeather senior meteorologist Jason Nicholls.
Heavy rain is expected to affect Taiwan from Thursday night (Oct. 22) into Saturday (Oct. 24) and east-central China from Friday night (Oct. 23) through Sunday (Oct. 25). Rainfall is forecast to total up to 18 inches, with the heaviest rain expected in northeastern Taiwan.
The heavy rain could cause flooding, mudslides, structural damage and transportation delays, according to AccuWeather.
Strong winds from Champi, with wind gusts up to 120 mph, are expected to affect Taiwan and eastern China from Thursday night into Sunday. The winds could cause structural damage, prolonged power outages and transportation delays.

articles.title_orig: iPhone Duo Reviewers Really Miss Face ID
articles.title_zh: iPhone Duo Reviewers Really Miss Face ID
articles.content_orig:
Touch ID on the iPhone Duo might end up being frustrating for some users, based on media reviews that came out today. Multiple reviewers found ‌Touch ID‌ to be slow to unlock, which can be jarring coming from Face ID .
According to Marques Brownlee , Apple added an intentional delay to "every single" ‌Touch ID‌ unlock. After you touch a finger to the side button to unlock, it pauses on the Lock Screen. If you keep your finger there, it continues to the Home Screen .
It's technically smart. Like, it's giving people a chance to check to see their notifications real quick before it goes and unlocks it. And if they want to deliberately hold it longer, it'll unlock. But as someone who is used to the instant unlocks from Face ID, I was like, I need to find a way to turn this off. And I did not find that. Like it just makes the fingerprint reader feel slow when it's not slow [...]
I really think Face ID is going to be the number one thing people miss coming from other iPhones.
Brownlee says his workaround is to wake the ‌iPhone Duo‌, swipe up, then touch the sensor for an instant unlock.
Engadget described ‌Touch ID‌ as taking "a bit longer to unlock than you might expect." Apple told the site that the ‌Touch ID‌ pause creates a more consistent experience when compared to other devices that use ‌Touch ID‌, like Macs and iPads, and gives the phone time to wake up and display Lock Screen notifications.
In her review , Joanna Stern said she was fumbling unlocks even a week in, with five fingers registered. "‌Face ID‌, I cannot tell you how deeply I miss you," she said.
Mrwhosetheboss said the hold instead of the tap "feels like a tiny bit of extra friction 50 times a day." He found ‌Touch ID‌ could be problematic just after washing his hands or with slightly greasy fingers, plus he said it's really only comfortable to use in landscape orientation.
PetaPixel said Apple's choice to use ‌Touch ID‌ instead of ‌Face ID‌ "was a mistake," and found it to be slower than ‌Face ID‌. Accidental presses when picking up or moving the iPhone also trigger a haptic error buzz. PetaPixel said it was buzzing constantly.
Apple allows the ‌iPhone Duo‌ to be unlocked with the Apple Watch as an alternative to ‌Touch ID‌, and PetaPixel said this method of unlocking was faster than using ‌Touch ID‌. Having a watch for unlocking "removed a lot of the friction" caused by ‌Touch ID‌.
Brian Tong said ‌Touch ID‌ feels like a step back. "I'm going to tell you right now, you will want to wear an Apple Watch," he said.
Gizmodo 's Raymond Wong said he missed ‌Face ID‌ every time he grabbed the ‌iPhone Duo‌ off a desk or out of a pocket and he remembered he had to put a registered finger on the button for unlocking. He said it was difficult to get used to not being able to look to authenticate a payment with Apple Pay . Wong also points out that as with old iPhones, winter gloves will need to come off for unlocking.
The Verge said "a week" was long enough to get used to ‌Touch ID‌, and that it's "mostly painless once you remember you're supposed to be using it." 9to5Mac said the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s biggest tradeoff might be ‌Touch ID‌, but also described it as working "quickly and reliably."
If you're getting an ‌iPhone Duo‌, will you miss ‌Face ID‌? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title_orig: El Salvador’s President Issues Harsh Warning to Haitian Gangs After 4 Soldiers Are Abducted
articles.title_zh: El Salvador’s President Issues Harsh Warning to Haitian Gangs After 4 Soldiers Are Abducted
articles.content_orig:
El Salvador has initiated a military operation to rescue four Salvadoran soldiers abducted by gangs in Haiti, President Nayib Bukele announced in a post on X, without elaborating.
Bukele, known for his intense crackdown on gang violence in El Salvador, warned in Wednesday’s statement that a more forceful response was coming if the personnel were not released alive and well.
“Do not take our word for empty threats,” the president wrote, addressing the gangs allegedly responsible for holding the four men. “We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too.”
Gangs in Haiti opened fire on an armoured vehicle carrying the men three days earlier, in the first major attack since an international gang suppression force began operating in the violence-wracked Caribbean country last year.
The four men, aviation technicians with the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), have been missing since they fled the burning vehicle in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets, Port-au-Prince.
Haiti’s government issued a news release on Wednesday evening saying the release of the abducted soldiers was an “absolute priority”.
It was not immediately clear if Haitian authorities received any confirmation that the Salvadoran soldiers are alive.
The government said a meeting was held at the prime minister’s office “to assess the ongoing interventions and determine the necessary measures to strengthen operations, in close collaboration with the Gang Repression Force”.
A spokesperson for the GSF did not immediately respond to a message seeking details
The UN-backed force is still fighting gangs in the community where Sunday’s attack occurred, warning residents in the area to remain indoors.
No one has claimed responsibility for the attack on the Salvadoran troops, which comes as Haiti prepares for its first general election in more than a decade. It also showcases the power of the gangs that control an estimated 70 percent of the capital, Port-au-Prince.
El Salvador is among several countries – including Chad, Jamaica and Guatemala – to form part of the gang suppression force, with more than 2,000 troops on the ground in Haiti.
Gang violence has displaced nearly 1.5 million people in Haiti in recent years. More than 5,700 people have been killed or injured from January through mid-September this year, and more than 230 have been kidnapped, according to the UN.
The area where the armoured vehicle was targeted is controlled by gangs, including Chèn Méchan; Kraze Barye, led by Vitel’Homme Innocent; and 400 Mawozo, led by Lanmo Sanjou.
Both gang leaders have been sanctioned by the UN and the US.

AI companies for years have promised that smarter models would be worth the staggering cost to build them. Anthropic on Wednesday made that case in cash.
Why it matters: As Wall Street broadly spent the day fearing an AI bubble, Anthropic offered what investors have been desperate to see: evidence that frontier AI can be a sustainable business .

Zoom in: Consider just one of the stats reported by Anthropic: The company is cash flow positive even as some of the world's most profitable companies are struggling to keep their AI spending in check.
Yes, but: The company's blistering pace of growth appeared to slow compared with the difference between the first and second quarters, when sales more than doubled.
Between the lines: Anthropic's latest financial disclosures reinforce what analysts and investors have been telling Axios:
Flashback: Anthropic's early bets on coding expertise, business customers and spending discipline have paid off.
Reality check: Anthropic hasn't solved every financial challenge associated with the AI buildout.
What we're watching: Whether Anthropic can sustain its technological and financial advantages as it expands its frontier intelligence offerings into additional niche areas beyond coding.
The bottom line: Anthropic is showing Wall Street how frontier intelligence can turn into an actual business right when investors needed some good news.
